_note: Baseline shell_execute verbs pre-approved for the Personal audience.
netclaw matches these as command prefixes, the same way the live
tool-approvals.json records them.
Source 1: the permissions.allow list from a Claude Code workspace
settings.json, translated from its syntax (Bash(x:*) -> x).
WebSearch, WebFetch(domain:...) and mcp__* entries are dropped:
netclaw governs those through AllowedTools and MCP grants, not
shell_execute.
Source 2: binaries newly available via /tools.
rtk-prefixed twins are included because rtk is now on PATH and is the
token-cheap path for read-heavy commands.
git push and git commit are deliberately absent: they are in the source
file's 'ask' list, not 'allow'.
Broader than the rest, inherited from the dev sandbox where a human
watches every call -- revisit if netclaw runs unattended on a schedule:
sops        decrypts secrets (whole binary, not a read-only subset)
curl        arbitrary network egress
sed/mv/mkdir mutating; sed -i can rewrite any readable file
Never seeded (mutate infrastructure or data): kubectl apply/delete/edit,
helm install/upgrade, terraform apply/destroy, aws write APIs, psql,
tcpdump, rsync.
